timeline_reviews.summary: Serial CLI transport stream accounted for as non-semantic transport; semantic actions come from the raw agent ledger.
Serial raw trajectory read: single-agent probing and partial core module implementation with no delegation or final entrypoint.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the six-argument Python markdown program, exact CLI behavior, multiple markdown extension phases, XHTML final phase, pure Node ESM, and required /output/test19.mjs deliverable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent launched a 13-agent md-spec-extract workflow, then tracked six tasks for specs, foundation modules, core engine, extensions, Pygments, and fuzz verification while keeping local implementation responsibility.
parallel.implementation: Produced partial /output/lib/md foundation files such as util, etree, serializer, stash, registry, and htmlparser, but did not complete the markdown engine, extensions, Pygments compatibility, or entrypoint.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No integrated runnable package was assembled; artifact validation listed only lib/md support modules and explicitly expected missing test19.mjs.
parallel.verification: Performed executable probes and planned differential fuzzing, but no final integrated node-vs-executable verification of a delivered test19.mjs occurred.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with child agents stalled or interrupted, final response was empty, and the official evaluator recorded 0/70 with solution_passed false.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Python markdown transformation chain, argument parsing, extension behavior, XHTML output, and need to produce Node.js code in /output.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single-agent plan with no workflow or subagents, first probing behavior and then directly building the core library files under /output/lib/core.
serial.implementation: Wrote partial core modules including chars, strings, element, serializer, htmlparser, blockparser, blockprocessors, and inlinepatterns, but did not finish extensions or entrypoint.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No final runnable test19.mjs was assembled; artifact validation listed only lib/core modules and marked the expected entrypoint absent.
serial.verification: Ran probes against the executable while implementing, but no completed end-to-end evaluator-aligned run of a Node entrypoint occurred before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt timed out after partial implementation, had an empty final response, and the official evaluator recorded 0/70 with solution_passed false.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the CLI arguments, Markdown phases, extensions, XHTML final output, no external npm dependency, and final test19.mjs requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and worked from the identical prompt and recognized the same task obligations while probing the executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both failed at delivery rather than because one had a different prompt or task understanding.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into a spec workflow plus tracked local tasks for foundation, core, extensions, Pygments, and fuzz verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one local implementation stream without workflow calls or child ownership boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child-result and failure-takeover obligations; serial avoided those coordination boundaries but still left implementation unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs contained detailed probe instructions and shared harness rules, but most findings never reached a usable aggregate handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probe findings and implementation context in one trajectory, with no cross-agent interface handoff.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a workflow-result boundary that serial did not; the observed problem is result/failure lifecycle rather than a missing requirement in the briefs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote initial lib/md utilities, tree, serializer, stash, registry, and html parser while relying on the spec workflow for broad behavior coverage.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a different lib/core foundation and advanced into block and inline processors, still without the final program entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent substantial work in workflow-backed probing and foundation modules; serial stayed in one implementation path and reached more core parser files, but neither completed the executable surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The spec workflow was launched in the background, retried stalled children, and ended killed with null aggregate result and no parent takeover of unfinished scope.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; status confirms zero workflow calls and no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel depended on child work that failed to return cleanly, while serial had only local unfinished work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel artifact validation found only lib/md support files and no expected test19.mjs; no completed final tree was assembled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifact validation found only lib/core support files and no expected test19.mjs; no submitted entrypoint existed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file sets differ by implementation namespace and content, but both converge on the same missing deliverable state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned differential fuzz verification, but the delivered artifact never reached an evaluator-aligned acceptance check for a Node entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed behavior and built modules, but likewise never produced a Node entrypoint for whole-task acceptance before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had verification in the task plan and probe workflow; serial had local probes. Neither converted verification into a passing delivered artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full cell budget, had returncode 143, and the workflow state recorded many stalled retries and killed status.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also consumed the full cell budget and timed out with returncode 143, but without workflow or subagent overhead.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both suffered timeout closure; only parallel had a child-work failure propagation chain before the same official failure outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations make this a both_fail pair. Both artifacts were missing the expected test19.mjs and both scored 0/70, so there is no official pass/fail discordance to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel launched a large spec-extraction workflow whose killed/stalled child work was not taken over, while serial stayed single-agent and directly wrote partial core modules. Both stopped before packaging an entrypoint.
parallel_contributors: Killed spec-extraction workflow with null result and stalled or interrupted child probes left required behavioral scope unfinished.
Artifact validation found only partial lib/md modules and no expected test19.mjs entrypoint.
serial_contributors: Single-agent implementation wrote partial lib/core modules but timed out before assembling test19.mjs.
Serial control had no delegation, so its failure is ordinary incomplete implementation and packaging rather than child-work propagation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel and serial used different partial module namespaces, lib/md versus lib/core.
Serial reached block and inline processor source files while parallel focused on workflow-backed probing and foundation files.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel-side adverse process consequence only

candidates.reason: The parallel plan assigned implementation-oriented work to the parent and tracked core engine and extension tasks; missing output resulted from unfinished execution, not absent implementation ownership.
No completed independently owned components reached a reconciliation point with incompatible interfaces; the run stalled before integration rather than leaving integration ownerless.
The prompt and parent trajectory retained responsibility for producing /output/test19.mjs; the missing entrypoint is a closure/takeover failure, not proof that assembly had no owner.
The parent created an end-to-end task list including implementation, extensions, Pygments, and differential verification; the pipeline was not unowned.
Implementation writes began while the probe workflow ran; productive work was not blocked behind a single mandatory serial preflight.
The parallel investigation used overlapping probe agents and overlapped with parent module writing, so this was not a completed serial investigation phase before implementation.
The critical path was harmed by failed or cancelled child work not being taken over; that direct failure-propagation boundary is more specific than generic underallocation.
The 13-agent fan-out consumed time, but it is the same stalled workflow chain as the retained no-takeover episode, so it is suppressed rather than double-labeled.
Some child prompts were broad, but no single oversized child has a distinct consequence apart from the shared stalled/cancelled workflow chain.
The child briefs were detailed and included task, harness, source-of-truth, and output rules; no already-known requirement is shown missing from a child brief and then causing unusable work.
The delegated work was mainly behavioral specification probing, and no completed independently produced components are shown to be incompatible because of an omitted interface contract.
No known finding is shown to disappear through summary or transfer before a receiver repeats work or acts without it.
The parent did not receive an excessive completed handoff and fail to reduce it; the workflow did not return a completed aggregate result.
No receiver consumed a superseded handoff or acted on stale workspace state.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts are visible at a parent decision point.
The parent did not make a whole-task completion or acceptance decision; the final response is empty and status shows the evaluator failure afterward.
Workflow stall retries occurred, but the evidence does not show a replacement repeating prior useful work because it lacked a checkpoint; the direct failure is no parent takeover.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Child interruptions are visible, but the most specific corrective boundary is that the parent did not resume, reassign, or take over the failed scope before closure.
No complete runnable candidate or compatible component set was available for late promotion; only partial modules and unfinished child work existed.
No child result or implementation change was merged after integrated verification, and there was no successful integrated verification loop.
No completed delegated implementation was retrievable and then left unjoined; the delegated workflow was still killed or in progress.
The planned verifier/fuzz stage did not produce a concrete completed finding trapped below the parent before closure.

The parent launched a required workflow, the workflow was killed with stalled in-progress probe agents and null result, several child trajectories show interruption, and the parent closed without taking over the unfinished scope or producing test19.mjs.
candidates.realized_consequence: Required delegated probe/spec scope remained unfinished and no parent takeover produced the required test19.mjs deliverable.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child interruptions are part of the episode, but the missing corrective action was parent takeover of failed or cancelled scope before closure.

candidates.reason: No concrete completed child result sufficient for implementation was visible to the parent and ignored; the notable returned material was partial probe/spec output.
The parent performed local implementation work and the workflow recorded progress/stalls; the same chain is better captured by failed child work not being taken over.
Parallel actors wrote probes/spec fragments and parent modules, but no competing implementation paths with overlapping behavior required reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file and observing or reconciling each other.
No source module produced or owned by one actor was replaced by another actor.
The required executable entrypoint test19.mjs was never present, so it could not have been overwritten.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced another actor's final-tree work.
Although actors used shared /tmp and /output areas, no unstable-state or provenance problem from unisolated writes is directly evidenced.
No generated artifact, cache, temporary file, or auxiliary implementation from one actor is shown contaminating another actor's execution or verification.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent delegated required behavioral probing to a workflow, then did not resume, reassign, or take over killed and interrupted child scope before the run closed.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel artifact contained only partial lib/md modules and no test19.mjs entrypoint after the killed workflow left required scope unfinished.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The visible interruptions are downstream evidence, but the retained boundary is the missing parent takeover after those failures rather than termination alone.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination, Critical-Path Starvation, Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Oversized Child Task, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered for the stalled workflow chain but suppressed in favor of No Failure Takeover.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no additional independent parallel-side episode cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only one label is retained because the timeout, child interruption, stalled retry, and missing entrypoint evidence form one propagation chain with one corrective boundary.
